title: Fun Run, Michael Scott Fun Run
logline: Michael turns the Scranton Community Center charity fun run into a tribute to himself, while Pam's art show forces her to tell Roy the truth and Darryl reminds Michael that the warehouse says yes only when it's asked.
outline: A: Michael's charity fun run (bibs with his face, a bid on Pam's paintings, a bullhorn speech) with Darryl as the warehouse voice of reason. B: Pam's art show at the Community Center; she tells Roy she is not happy and does not want June 14. C: Dwight and Andy's Thursday turns with a stopwatch, Stanley stuck at 187 with Creed. Order: cold, A, B, C, A, C, A, B, C, A, B, tag.
theme: Being present versus being the one everyone is looking at: who you show up for when the spotlight is on you.
storySoFar: Jim is in Stamford dating Shannon and working with Karen; his unanswered card sits in Pam's drawer beside the Stamford paints and her napkin answer. Pam has told Roy she is not happy; June 14 is still on. Pam's Tuesday watercolor class at the Scranton Community Center is known to Michael, who promised to keep quiet, or maybe not. Michael's Scranton Community Center Fun Run is now his big charity project, with bibs bearing his face. Dwight and Andy share the Pruitt account and speak in four-minute turns on Thursday. Stanley is stuck at 187 days; Michael's joke dies, and Kevin closes with "Nobody say nothing." Andy's banjo hold music still annoys Toby, and Toby's Rule Fourteen stands.

extras.name: Lorraine Dupree
extras.title: Director, Scranton Community Center
extras.voice: Brisk, grateful, a little unimpressed by Michael. Speaks in clipboard phrases: 'Sign-up sheet,' 'Silent auction,' 'Please, no more bibs.'

stateChanges.progress: Pam tells Roy after the art show that she is not happy and does not want June 14; Roy walks off to think. Engagement not yet formally ended; finale is the ending and Jim's card answer.

stateChanges.arc: Michael Wants to Be the Favorite
stateChanges.progress: Michael's fun run turns into a self-tribute (Michael Scott bibs, a Michael Scott Collection bid on Pam's paintings) but he means well; he gives the mic to Pam and covers his ears on her Tuesday class.

stateChanges.arc: Dwight vs Andy for Number Two
stateChanges.progress: Thursday turns agreed at the break room table; Dwight goes over at the fun run start and Andy calls it out.
Still at 187. Creed's Dayton story goes unfollowed.

stateChanges.status: Pam told him she is not happy and does not want June 14; Roy is shaken and asks if it is Halpert.
Michael asked the warehouse; Darryl says ask first, that's the whole thing

stateChanges.text: Pam's windmill painting has a Michael Scott Collection sign taped on it; Michael bid on every painting for the fun run.
Pam told the fun run crowd she takes Tuesday classes at the Community Center; Michael covered his ears and said he's not Jim.
Pam's napkin answer to Jim still sits folded in her drawer; she says she will say it herself, in person.
Michael's 'That's what she said' dies to Stanley's countdown at 187; Kevin closes with 'Nobody say nothing.'
Oscar: 'Actually, that's a banjo on hold.' Andy's bear-paw phone plays banjo hold music.
Michael calls his bid kindness disgusting, the Jan callback.

scenes.recap: Stanley is still at 187 and Michael's joke dies on silence until Kevin closes it.

beats.text: One hundred and eighty-seven days.
A hundred and eighty-seven. Stanley, that's what she said.

beats.caption: Stanley stares at his crossword. Nobody moves.

beats.text: Nobody say nothing.

beats.caption: answers his bear-paw phone, which begins playing banjo hold music

beats.text: Actually, Andy, that's a banjo on hold.

scenes.recap: Michael announces the Michael Scott Fun Run for the Community Center, and the warehouse and the fire code push back.

beats.text: Scranton! I have a vision. The Michael Scott Fun Run, Saturday, for the Community Center Arts Fund.
Is it a fun run for you, or a fun run for us? Because I'm wearing heels.
Every bib says Michael Scott Fun Run. Bibs are very important.

lines: I'm not doing this for me. I'm doing it for the arts. Also my face is on the bibs, and it's a good face.

beats.text: Actually, the Community Center already has an arts fund. It's called a bake sale.
Public runs need a permit, and the parking lot needs a fire lane.
Toby, nobody asked the fire code to run.
My guys work Saturdays. Warehouse is not running. Ask me before you put anybody on a course.
Great. Warehouse, water stations. Perfect. Everybody gets a station.
Question: will there be a timing chip? Because I am course marshal, armed with a clipboard.

beats.caption: Toby stares at the fire code binder in his lap.

scenes.recap: Pam tells Roy her art show is Saturday and that she has something to say after it, while Kelly floats Stamford rumors.

beats.text: Saturday's my show. At the Community Center. Would you come?
Show of what?
Paintings. Mine.
Oh. Yeah. Sure. June fourteenth, the deposit's due, Pam.
After the show, Roy. I'll tell you something. I promise.
Ooh. Is this about Stamford? Because I heard you're moving to Stamford.
Pam's not moving to Stamford.
I'm not moving, Kelly. Roy, after the show.

lines: I've said 'it's fine' for a year. Saturday I'm going to say the thing out loud, in a room with my paintings in it.

beats.caption: Pam glances at her top drawer, where the card is.

scenes.recap: Dwight and Andy agree at the break room table to four-minute turns, and nobody goes over.

beats.caption: sets a stopwatch on the table with a loud click

beats.text: Thursday. Dale Pruitt. Four minutes each. Do you agree?
Four minutes each, Dwight. I'm a Cornell man. I can be concise.
False. You have never been concise. Begin.
Dale, good morning. The Pruitt account is a family. Like Cornell.
Kevin want four minute too. Four minute good.

lines: Dwight isn't my rival. He's an adversary with a stopwatch. I respect the stopwatch.

beats.text: Actually, Andy, your phone is playing banjo on hold again.
Four minutes. Nobody goes over.

beats.caption: Andy looks at the stopwatch. Dwight looks at Andy.

scenes.recap: Michael offers the warehouse his bib, and Darryl tells him to ask first.

beats.text: Darryl! I paid the registration for every warehouse employee. Two hundred and eleven dollars.
You paid for my guys to run?
I paid for your guys to be bibs. Michael Scott Fun Run, Warehouse Division.
Ask first, Michael. That's the whole thing.

beats.caption: Michael checks his coffee mug for the right answer.

beats.text: Would you like to run?
No.

lines: Michael treats my warehouse like a sales quota. Nobody on my dock is a quota. Ask them. Then listen to the no.

beats.text: Okay. Ask them. This is a growth moment for me.
Mm-hm. Water stations are fine. Get out of my dock.

scenes.recap: Stanley vents to Creed about his countdown, and Creed says something unsettling about Dayton that nobody follows up.

beats.text: One eighty-seven. Michael wants me to enjoy the fun run.
I ran a fun run in Dayton in 1971. The man who finished second is still there. He knows.

beats.caption: Stanley fills in a crossword square.

beats.text: Did I stutter?
Dayton's a nice town. Quiet, mostly.

scenes.recap: Michael bids on every one of Pam's paintings for the fun run, and makes it about the Michael Scott Collection.

beats.text: Mr. Scott, the paintings are for the silent auction. Bids go on the sheet.
I'll bid on all of them. For the fun run. The Michael Scott Collection.
Michael, you can't buy my paintings.
I'm buying the windmill. It's a good windmill. I'm keeping the arts program open.

beats.caption: tapes a sign reading MICHAEL SCOTT COLLECTION onto the windmill painting

beats.text: This is disgusting, I know. It's kindness. Jan's word.
That's very generous. Please, no more bibs.

beats.caption: Pam holds her brush like a weapon.

beats.text: You didn't have to do that.
I know. That's the part I'm good at.

scenes.recap: After the art show, Pam tells Roy she is not happy and does not want June 14, and Roy walks off to think.

beats.text: Your paintings are nice. What's the sign on the windmill?
It's Michael's. Roy, I need to tell you something. Not in front of the cheese.
Okay. Tell me.

beats.caption: Somewhere inside, Lorraine rings a bell for the silent…

beats.text: I'm not happy. I haven't been for a long time. I don't want June fourteenth.

lines: Roy's a good man. I told him I was staying in Scranton, and I didn't say it was with him. That was the coward version.

beats.text: Is it Halpert?
It's me, Roy. It's me.

beats.caption: Roy looks at the windmill with the sign on it.

beats.text: I need a minute. Pam, I need a whole minute.

scenes.recap: Dwight and Andy take turns at the fun run start line, and Dwight goes over four minutes.

beats.caption: clicks a stopwatch on the hood of his car

beats.text: Four minutes. Warm up the crowd. Go.

beats.caption: bursts into a cappella about the arts and Cornell

beats.text: That was a song. Songs are not minutes, Andy.
Dwight, I am not going over. Ask anyone.
False. You're at six.

lines: I have been Number Two since the day I was born. Andy has been Number Two since one Tuesday. Four minutes is generous.

scenes.recap: The fun run starts in chaos, Michael's bullhorn speech takes over, and he hands the mic to Pam, who mentions her Tuesday class.

beats.text: Runners! Walkers! Anyone who has ever been a Michael!

beats.caption: fires a party popper that sprays streamers into Toby's face

beats.text: Michael, that's not a starter. That's a fire hazard.

beats.caption: sprints off toward the entrance, cones flying behind him

beats.text: He's going the wrong way. The finish is the other way.

beats.caption: Toby sighs at the cones.

beats.text: Okay, who wants to hear a speech? Me. It's about me. Kidding. Pam, come up here.
Thank you, everyone. The Community Center's arts program is the reason I paint. I take Tuesday classes there.

beats.caption: covers both ears and says loudly, I'm not Jim

beats.text: I didn't hear that. I'm not Jim. I'm not hearing it.
Michael, that's disgusting. Standing up for Pam is so disgusting.

scenes.recap: Back at reception, Pam says she will answer Jim herself, and Michael promises to keep out of it.

beats.text: Do you want me to call Jim? I can call Jim. I'm great on phones.
No. I'm going to say it myself. In person.
Okay. I'm not going to say anything. I'm present. Look at me being present.

beats.caption: Pam takes the napkin from her drawer and folds it again.

beats.text: Thanks, Michael. For the paintings. Even the windmill.

scenes.recap: After hours, Stanley is still at 187, and Michael tries the joke once more before Kevin closes it.

beats.text: Stanley, a hundred and eighty-seven. You're still here. That's what she said.

beats.caption: Stanley does not look up from his crossword.

beats.text: Did I stutter?
Nobody say nothing.
